skill.name: research-storage
skill.description: Defines consistent directories, filenames, Markdown templates, and lookup rules for saving and reusing dokhak research results.
skill.summary: Organize cached research with canonical paths, reusable templates, and legacy-aware directory lookup.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: All 81 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, template placeholders, and a malformed obfuscation heuristic. The skill contains readable storage guidance and no command execution, reconnaissance, obfuscation, or prompt injection behavior.

static_findings.snippet: > Glob does NOT return directories. All patterns MUST end with a filename (e.g., `/research.md`).
> | `.research/sections/*9-1*/*` | ✅ Returns all files in matching dirs |
This catches slug variations like `Core-Concepts`, `core_concepts`, etc.
Used by `researcher` agent for path resolution:
| `.research/` directory missing | Auto-create on first write          |

content.value_statement: Research agents can create inconsistent paths and formats, making cached results difficult to find and reuse. This skill standardizes storage, naming, templates, and directory resolution.
actual_capabilities: Defines canonical .research/init and .research/sections structures for shared research files.
Normalizes chapter and section identifiers and creates lowercase kebab-case slugs.
Builds canonical paths for section research and source registries.
Resolves legacy directory names through four ordered Glob lookup tiers.
Supplies Markdown templates for summaries, sources, and section research.
Standardizes XML result, resolution, and coverage formats for agent communication.
limitations: Provides conventions and pseudocode, not executable normalization or resolution functions.
Stores files locally and does not perform web research or verify cited sources.
Flexible wildcard lookup can return an unintended legacy match when similar directories exist.
Assumes agents can use Read, Write, and Glob within the current project.

use_cases.title: Maintain a research cache
use_cases.description: Store initial and section research in predictable locations with consistent Markdown formats.

use_cases.title: Reuse sources while writing
use_cases.description: Locate existing findings and source registries before drafting a section.

use_cases.title: Migrate inconsistent folders
use_cases.description: Resolve legacy directory names and identify their canonical replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Save initial research
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize this research about {topic} in the standard init cache. Create summary and source registry content using the documented templates.

prompt_templates.title: Store section findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Create canonical storage paths for chapter {chapter}, section {section}, titled {title}. Format the supplied findings for research.md and sources.md.
prompt_templates.scenario: Saving research for one planned section.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve existing research
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve stored research for chapter {chapter}, section {section}, titled {title}. Apply lookup tiers in order and report the matched path, existence, and tier.
prompt_templates.scenario: Finding reusable research with inconsistent legacy names.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the research cache
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the .research directory for naming inconsistencies, incomplete subtopic coverage, and duplicate legacy matches. Propose canonical paths without deleting or overwriting files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Maintaining a large cache across multiple agents.

output_examples.input: Store chapter 1, section 02, titled Core Concepts.
output_examples.output: Canonical directory: .research/sections/01-2-core-concepts/. Research content goes in research.md, and citations go in sources.md.

output_examples.input: Find research for chapter 01, section 2, titled Core Concepts.
output_examples.output: Existing research found through the canonical exact-match tier at .research/sections/01-2-core-concepts/.

output_examples.input: Prepare initial research files for a new project.
output_examples.output: Create .research/init/summary.md for concepts and learning paths. Create .research/init/sources.md for accepted, secondary, and rejected sources.

best_practices: Keep chapter identifiers two digits, section identifiers unpadded, and slugs lowercase.
Record every accepted and rejected source with reliability and verification details.
Run lookup tiers in order and stop after the first unambiguous match.
anti_patterns: Do not create new directories with legacy or mixed naming formats.
Do not use directory-only Glob patterns when checking for stored research.
Do not overwrite partial research before checking its subtopic coverage.

faq.question: Does this skill perform research?
faq.answer: No. It defines how other agents store, locate, and format research results.

faq.question: Where is initial project research stored?
faq.answer: Initial summaries and source registries are stored under .research/init/.

faq.question: How are section directories named?
faq.answer: Use a two-digit chapter, an unpadded section, and a lowercase kebab-case slug.

faq.question: Can it find legacy directory names?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents four ordered Glob strategies for canonical and legacy variations.

faq.question: Which files does it define?
faq.answer: It defines summary.md, research.md, and sources.md templates for cached research.

faq.question: Should cached research be committed?
faq.answer: The skill recommends ignoring .research/ because its contents are regenerable.
